title: A Dual Mechanism-Based Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model for Predicting Mitoxantrone and Liposomal Mitoxantrone Disposition: Preclinical Validation in Rats and Human Extrapolation with Clinical Evaluation.
authors: Xu, Yuxiang; Li, Shuo; Yang, Zhixuan; Qiu, Yushuo; Dong, Jiameng; Gao, Xiaonan; Gao, Jinglin; Feng, Zhangying; Wang, Mingxia
one_liner_zh: 该文构建米托蒽醌及脂质体制剂的生理药代动力学模型，聚焦药物组织分布与药代预测，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model to quantitatively predict plasma and tissue concentrations of both liposomal-encapsulated and free mitoxantrone in rats and further extrapolate the model to human clinical scenarios. METHODS: A dual-compartment PBPK framework was constructed to separately describe the disposition of liposomal carriers and released free mitoxantrone. Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) based on partial rank correlation coefficient (PRCC) was performed to identify key parameters. The external validation was evaluated using rat plasma pharmacokinetic and human clinical data from previous reported studies. Allometric scaling was applied to extrapolate the model to adult humans, and Monte Carlo simulation was utilized to predict clinical plasma concentrations under fixed clinical doses of 20, 30, and 40 mg in lymphoma patients. RESULTS: PRCC analysis results demonstrated that tissue DNA binding capacity (T_DNA) and tissue-to-plasma liposome partition coefficient (Kp_n) were the most dominant parameters governing free drug and liposomal exposure, respectively (PRCC > 0.9). Overall average absolute fold error (AAFE) for tissue predictions was below 2.0. A slightly higher AAFE of 2.16 was observed for free drug submodel, which still complied with the widely accepted 3-fold error threshold for PBPK validation. Model external validation results also demonstrated acceptable predictive capacity of the model for both total and free mitoxantrone concentrations across preclinical and clinical dose levels (AAFE < 3). For human extrapolation, over 92% of clinically observed plasma concentrations from 37 lymphoma patients fell within the model's 90% predictive interval. CONCLUSION: This study established a robust, mechanism-driven PBPK model that distinguished encapsulated and free mitoxantrone disposition. The model achieved reliable prediction performance and effectively interprets pharmacokinetic characteristics of PEGylated liposomal mitoxantrone. The present framework provided a valuable mechanistic reference for the construction and optimization of liposomal mitoxantrone PBPK models and supported future translational pharmacokinetic studies of liposomal formulations.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在建立生理药代动力学（PBPK）模型，以定量预测脂质体包裹和游离米托蒽醌在大鼠血浆和组织中的浓度，并进一步将该模型外推至人类临床场景。方法：构建双室PBPK框架，分别描述脂质体载体和释放的游离米托蒽醌的处置过程。基于偏秩相关系数（PRCC）的全局敏感性分析（GSA）用于识别关键参数。外部验证使用既往研究报告的大鼠血浆药代动力学和人类临床数据进行评估。采用异速缩放将模型外推至成人，并利用蒙特卡洛模拟预测淋巴瘤患者在固定临床剂量20、30和40 mg下的临床血浆浓度。结果：PRCC分析结果表明，组织DNA结合能力（T_DNA）和组织-血浆脂质体分配系数（Kp_n）分别是控制游离药物和脂质体暴露的最主要参数（PRCC > 0.9）。组织预测的总体平均绝对折叠误差（AAFE）低于2.0。游离药物子模型观察到略高的AAFE为2.16，但仍符合PBPK验证广泛接受的3倍误差阈值。模型外部验证结果也表明，该模型对临床前和临床剂量水平下总米托蒽醌和游离米托蒽醌浓度均具有可接受的预测能力（AAFE < 3）。对于人类外推，来自37名淋巴瘤患者的临床观察血浆浓度中，超过92%落在模型的90%预测区间内。结论：本研究建立了一个稳健的、机制驱动的PBPK模型，能够区分包裹和游离米托蒽醌的处置过程。该模型实现了可靠的预测性能，并有效解释了聚乙二醇化脂质体米托蒽醌的药代动力学特征。本框架为脂质体米托蒽醌PBPK模型的构建和优化提供了有价值的机制参考，并支持未来脂质体制剂的转化药代动力学研究。
